category: PCB design rules: Electrical, Routing, SMT, Mask, Plane & Testpoint types
description: Individual PCB design rule types from the Electrical, Routing, SMT, Mask, Plane and Testpoint categories of Design > Rules (PCB Rules and Constraints Editor) or the Constraint Manager, plus the mechanics of rule scoping, priority, import/export and the DRC options that act on them.

tools.name: Short-Circuit (Electrical rule)
tools.description: Tests for copper of different nets touching on any signal or plane layer. Normally one rule scoped All-All with Allow Short Circuit disabled; additional rules with Allow Short Circuit enabled are used where an intentional short is required (e.g. a net-tie footprint or an analog/digital ground bridge). Checked by online DRC, batch DRC and the autorouter.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Electrical > Short-Circuit; binary scope (Where The First/Second Object Matches)

parameters.name: Allow Short Circuit
parameters.description: When enabled, objects matched by the two scopes may overlap without a violation.

tools.example: Rule 'ShortCircuit_NetTie': First object InComponent('NT1'), second object All, Allow Short Circuit = enabled, priority 1. Default rule 'ShortCircuit' All/All, disabled.
tools.notes: Prefer Net Tie component types (with Verify Shorting Copper in the DRC report options) over blanket short-circuit exemptions. Query keyword IsRule_ShortCircuit selects these rules.

tools.name: Un-Routed Net (Electrical rule)
tools.description: Reports nets whose connections are not completely routed (open connections still shown as ratsnest lines). With Check for incomplete connections enabled it also tests track/arc-to-track/arc, track-to-via, track-to-pad, via-to-pad, via-to-via and polygon connectivity so that copper that only appears to touch is flagged. Batch DRC only.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Electrical > Un-Routed Net; unary scope

parameters.name: Check for incomplete connections
parameters.description: Enables the geometric connectivity sub-checks in addition to the ratsnest test.

tools.example: Keep the default 'UnRoutedNet' rule (scope All) enabled and run Tools > Design Rule Check with Sub-Net Details enabled to list the unrouted pins of each net.
tools.notes: Several other checks (e.g. Net Antennae) rely on this rule being enabled. Query keyword IsRule_BrokenNets selects it.

tools.name: Un-Connected Pin (Electrical rule)
tools.description: Flags component pads that have no net assigned and no connecting copper. Use it to catch pins that were left unconnected on the schematic by mistake; scope it to specific component classes or footprints to exclude mechanical pads and mounting holes. Has no constraint fields.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Electrical > Un-Connected Pin; unary scope
tools.example: Rule scoped InComponentClass('ICs') so that only integrated-circuit pins without nets are reported; not enabled by default.
tools.notes: Online and batch DRC. Query keyword IsRule_UnconnectedPin selects it.

tools.name: Modified Polygon (Electrical rule)
tools.description: Detects polygon pours that are shelved, or that have been modified (moved, edited outline, net changed) but not yet repoured, so stale copper cannot reach fabrication outputs. Both conditions can be allowed individually.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Electrical > Modified Polygon; unary scope

parameters.name: Allow shelved
parameters.description: Suppresses violations for shelved polygons.

parameters.name: Allow modified
parameters.description: Suppresses violations for polygons with pending outline/net changes.

tools.example: Before generating Gerbers run a batch DRC with this rule enabled; fix violations with Tools > Polygon Pours > Repour All (or Repour Modified).
tools.notes: Online and batch DRC. Related: Tools > Polygon Pours > Shelve / Restore, Polygon Manager.

tools.name: Creepage Distance (Electrical rule)
tools.description: Checks the surface path length between conductors of different nets, following the board surface around unplated holes, slots, cutouts and board edges, against a minimum creepage value. Used for mains/high-voltage isolation barriers where a straight-line clearance rule is insufficient. Not created by default.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Electrical > Creepage Distance; binary scope

parameters.name: Creepage distance
parameters.description: Minimum surface path length between the two scopes.

parameters.name: Ignore Internal Layers
parameters.description: Restrict the check to outer layers.

parameters.name: Apply to Polygon Pour
parameters.description: Include polygon copper in the check.

tools.example: First object InNetClass('MAINS_L_N'), second object InNetClass('SELV'), creepage 8 mm; add a slot cutout under the isolator to lengthen the surface path.
tools.notes: Online and batch DRC and obeyed by routing. Query keyword IsRule_Creepage.

tools.name: Z-Axis Clearance (Electrical rule)
tools.description: Tests the vertical (through-the-stack) clearance between copper objects of different nets on different layers, for example a trace directly above a plane cut or embedded copper in thin dielectrics. A beta feature enabled through the Advanced Settings flag PCB.Rules.ZAxisClearanceRule.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Electrical > Z-Axis Clearance; binary scope (requires PCB.Rules.ZAxisClearanceRule)

parameters.name: Z-Axis Clearance
parameters.description: Minimum vertical distance between the two matched object sets.

tools.example: Enable PCB.Rules.ZAxisClearanceRule in Preferences > System > General > Advanced, restart, then add a Z-Axis Clearance rule between InNetClass('HV') and All with 0.2 mm.
tools.notes: Availability and behaviour may change between releases; verify in your version's rule reference.

tools.name: Routing Neck-Down (Routing rule)
tools.description: Limits the total length of trace routed narrower than the Width rule's Preferred Width (down to Min Width) on a net, so BGA escape necks stay short. Only available when PCB.Rules.RoutingNeckdown is enabled in Advanced Settings; violations are hatched on the trace.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Routing > Routing Neck-Down (requires PCB.Rules.RoutingNeckdown)

parameters.name: Neck-Down Length
parameters.description: Maximum accumulated narrow-trace length per net; can be set per layer.

tools.example: Width rule for InNetClass('DDR') Min 0.09 mm / Preferred 0.12 mm; Routing Neck-Down 3 mm so only the BGA breakout may use 0.09 mm.
tools.notes: Enable the rule for online/batch checking in the Design Rule Checker dialog after turning the advanced flag on.

tools.name: Routing Topology (Routing rule)
tools.description: Defines the pin-to-pin connection pattern the connection analyser uses for a net's ratsnest and the autorouter follows: Shortest (default), Horizontal, Vertical, Daisy-Simple, Daisy-MidDriven, Daisy-Balanced or Starburst. Daisy variants honour Source/Terminator pad settings; custom topologies are built with From-Tos.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Routing > Routing Topology; Constraint Manager: Electrical view > Topology

parameters.name: Topology
parameters.description: Shortest | Horizontal | Vertical | Daisy-Simple | Daisy-MidDriven | Daisy-Balanced | Starburst.

tools.example: Rule scoped InNetClass('CLK_TREE') with Topology = Daisy-MidDriven; set the driver pad as Source in the PCB panel (Nets mode) so the ratsnest branches from the middle.
tools.notes: Non-Shortest topologies slow connection analysis on big nets; custom From-To topologies are limited to nets with 20 pads or fewer. Checked by batch DRC.

tools.name: Routing Priority (Routing rule)
tools.description: Assigns a 0-100 priority to nets so the autorouter processes higher-priority nets first (critical clocks and differential pairs before general signals). Has no effect on interactive routing or DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Routing > Routing Priority (Constraint Manager: Advanced rule)

parameters.name: Routing Priority
parameters.description: Integer 0-100; higher routes earlier.

tools.example: InNetClass('CLOCKS') priority 100, InNetClass('POWER') priority 50, default All priority 0, then Route > Auto Route > All.
tools.notes: Only meaningful with the legacy Situs autorouter or third-party routers.

tools.name: Routing Layers (Routing rule)
tools.description: Lists every signal layer with an Allow Routing checkbox, restricting which copper layers the matched nets may be routed on. The interactive router refuses layer changes to non-permitted layers and DRC flags existing copper on them. Layer routing direction (for the autorouter) is set separately in the Situs Layer Directions dialog.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Routing > Routing Layers; default rule required

parameters.name: Enabled Layers
parameters.description: Per-signal-layer Allow Routing checkbox.

tools.example: Rule InNetClass('RF') allowing only Top Layer, priority above the default 'RoutingLayers' rule that allows all layers.
tools.notes: Combine with Routing Via Style scoped by layer pair to control blind/buried usage.

tools.name: Routing Corners (Routing rule)
tools.description: Specifies the corner style (90 Degrees, 45 Degrees, Rounded) and setback range that a third-party autorouter should apply. The built-in Situs router uses 45-degree corners natively and does not consult this rule; interactive routing corner style is chosen with Shift+Space instead.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Routing > Routing Corners (Constraint Manager: Advanced rule)

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: 90 Degrees | 45 Degrees | Rounded.

parameters.name: Setback Min / Max
parameters.description: Corner setback range for 45 Degrees and Rounded styles.

tools.example: Style = Rounded, Setback Min 0.3 mm, Max 1 mm before exporting a Specctra .dsn for an external router.
tools.notes: Rarely needed in modern flows; keep for router export compatibility.

tools.name: Wire Bonding (Routing rule)
tools.description: Constrains bond wires in chip-on-board designs: minimum wire-to-wire distance between bond-wire 3D bodies, minimum and maximum wire length, and the margin a wire must keep from the edge of its bond finger pad. Checked by batch DRC only.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Routing > Wire Bonding (Constraint Manager: Advanced rule)

parameters.name: Wire To Wire
parameters.description: Minimum distance between adjacent bond wires.

parameters.name: Min Wire Length / Max Wire Length
parameters.description: Permitted bond-wire length range.

parameters.name: Bond Finger Margin
parameters.description: Minimum padding from the bond finger pad edge.

tools.example: Scope IsBondWire, Wire To Wire 0.1 mm, length 0.5-3 mm, margin 0.05 mm; verify with Tools > Design Rule Check.
tools.notes: Requires the Wire Bonding feature (die placement, bond wires) in the PCB editor; query keywords IsBondWire, IsBondFinger, IsBondWireConnected.

tools.name: SMD To Corner (SMT rule)
tools.description: Minimum straight distance from the edge of a surface-mount pad to the first routing corner, giving clean pad exits for assembly. The interactive router holds a straight exit segment of this length and collapses miters rather than violating it. Online DRC, batch DRC and interactive routing.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > SMT > SMD To Corner

parameters.name: Distance
parameters.description: Minimum pad-edge-to-first-corner distance.

tools.example: Rule InComponentClass('FinePitch') with Distance 0.25 mm; leave the default All rule at 0 to avoid over-constraining passives.
tools.notes: Interactive differential-pair routing prioritises coupling and may not honour it; use Quick Differential Pair Routing where strict compliance is required.

tools.name: SMD To Plane (SMT rule)
tools.description: Maximum routing length from the centre of an SMD pad to the centre of the via or pad that connects it to a power plane, keeping decoupling paths short. Online and batch DRC only.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > SMT > SMD To Plane

parameters.name: Distance
parameters.description: Maximum pad-centre to plane-connection-centre length.

tools.example: Scope InNet('GND') Or InNetClass('POWER') with Distance 1.5 mm to enforce short decoupling-capacitor stubs.
tools.notes: Only meaningful on boards with internal plane layers.

tools.name: SMD Neck-Down (SMT rule)
tools.description: Maximum ratio of the connecting track width to the SMD pad width, expressed as a percentage, preventing tracks as wide as the pad that would wick solder or hide tombstoning. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > SMT > SMD Neck-Down

parameters.name: Neck-Down
parameters.description: Track width as percentage of pad width (e.g. 50%).

tools.example: Default All rule 50%; a 100% rule scoped InNetClass('POWER') so wide power traces can enter power pads fully.
tools.notes: Interacts with Width rules: DRC compares the actual track width entering the pad with the pad's width.

tools.name: SMD Entry (SMT rule)
tools.description: Restricts the directions from which a track may enter or exit a single-layer SMD pad: Any Angle, Corner, or Side (the long side, when it is more than twice the end length). Pads can always be entered from either end. Applied by the interactive router as well as online/batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > SMT > SMD Entry

parameters.name: Any Angle
parameters.description: Allow entry at arbitrary angles.

parameters.name: Corner
parameters.description: Allow entry at pad corners.

parameters.name: Side
parameters.description: Allow entry through the long side of the pad.

tools.example: For IPC-A-610 style exits disable Any Angle and Corner so passives are only entered end-on or side-on; pair with SMD To Corner 0.2 mm.
tools.notes: Not created by default; differential-pair routing limitation as for SMD To Corner.

tools.name: Solder Mask Expansion (Mask rule)
tools.description: Sets how far the solder-mask opening at each pad and via is expanded (positive) or contracted (negative) radially from the copper land or, with Solder Mask From The Hole Edge, from the hole. Tented Top/Bottom options suppress the opening entirely so vias are covered. Values can differ per side and can be overridden per object in the Properties panel.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Mask > Solder Mask Expansion

parameters.name: Expansion Top / Bottom
parameters.description: Radial expansion; default 4 mil (0 when PCB.SolderMaskZeroExpansion is enabled).

parameters.name: Solder Mask From The Hole Edge
parameters.description: Measure from the hole perimeter instead of the copper edge.

parameters.name: Tented Top / Tented Bottom
parameters.description: No mask opening on that side.

tools.example: Default rule 0.05 mm; a second rule scoped IsVia And (HoleSize < 0.35mm) with Tented Top and Tented Bottom enabled to tent small vias.
tools.notes: Gerber/ODB++ mask layers are generated from this rule at output time; check Minimum Solder Mask Sliver for the resulting webs.

tools.name: Paste Mask Expansion (Mask rule)
tools.description: Defines the stencil aperture at each pad as the pad shape expanded/contracted by an absolute value or a percentage. Options control whether SMD pads receive paste and whether through-hole pads get top/bottom paste (pin-in-paste). Output to Gerber, Gerber X2, ODB++, IPC-2581, Draftsman and PCB prints.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Mask > Paste Mask Expansion

parameters.name: Use Paste For SMD Pads
parameters.description: Enable/disable paste on SMD pads.

parameters.name: Use Top Paste / Use Bottom Paste
parameters.description: Paste on through-hole pads per side.

parameters.name: Measure Method / Expansion
parameters.description: Absolute distance or percentage of pad size; negative shrinks the aperture.

tools.example: Default 0 mm; rule InComponentClass('QFN') Expansion -0.05 mm to shrink QFN apertures; rule for thermal pads using a custom paste-mask region instead.
tools.notes: Per-pad overrides and custom paste shapes are set in the pad's Properties panel; tracks, regions, fills and arcs can also carry paste-mask expansions.

tools.name: Power Plane Connect Style (Plane rule)
tools.description: Controls how a pin or via connects to an internal (negative) power plane: Relief Connect (thermal spokes), Direct Connect or No Connect, with conductor count (2/4), conductor width, air gap and expansion. Simple mode applies one style everywhere; Advanced mode allows per-layer definitions. Applied when plane layers are generated for output.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Plane > Power Plane Connect Style

parameters.name: Connect Style
parameters.description: Relief Connect | Direct Connect | No Connect.

parameters.name: Conductors / Conductor Width / Air-Gap / Expansion
parameters.description: Thermal relief geometry (Relief Connect only).

tools.example: Default rule Relief Connect, 4 conductors, 0.25 mm width, 0.25 mm air gap; a Direct Connect rule scoped IsVia for stitching vias on GND.
tools.notes: Distinct from Polygon Connect Style, which governs positive copper pours.

tools.name: Power Plane Clearance (Plane rule)
tools.description: Sets the radial anti-pad clearance created around pads and vias that pass through, but are not connected to, an internal power plane. Larger values reduce capacitive coupling; smaller values preserve plane copper under dense BGAs. Applied at output generation.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Plane > Power Plane Clearance

parameters.name: Clearance
parameters.description: Radial anti-pad clearance.

tools.example: Default 0.5 mm; rule scoped InComponent('U1') with 0.2 mm to keep the plane continuous under a 0.8 mm-pitch BGA.
tools.notes: Split-plane pullback (plane edge to board edge) is set in the Layer Stack Manager, not here.

tools.name: Polygon Connect Style (Plane rule)
tools.description: Defines how pads and vias of the polygon's net connect to a polygon pour on signal layers: Relief Connect, Direct Connect or No Connect, with air-gap width, conductor width, conductor count (2, 4, Auto or Min Distance) and rotation. Applied at pour time; pads with custom thermal reliefs are excluded.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Plane > Polygon Connect Style

parameters.name: Connect Style
parameters.description: Relief Connect | Direct Connect | No Connect.

parameters.name: Conductors / Conductor Width / Air Gap Width / Rotation
parameters.description: Thermal-relief geometry for Relief Connect.

tools.example: Default Relief Connect 4 x 0.25 mm; second rule scoped IsVia, Direct Connect, so vias in the GND pour are solid; repour with Tools > Polygon Pours > Repour All.
tools.notes: Change the rule then repour: existing polygons keep the old connection until repoured (Modified Polygon rule will flag them).

tools.name: Fabrication Testpoint Style (Testpoint rule)
tools.description: Physical requirements for pads/vias that may serve as bare-board test points: size and hole-size ranges, inter-testpoint spacing, component-body, board-edge and hole-centre clearances, an optional test grid (origin, size, tolerance), allowed side and whether points may sit under components. The Testpoint Manager, autorouter, DRC and outputs all obey it.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Testpoint > Fabrication Testpoint Style

parameters.name: Min / Max / Preferred Size and Hole Size
parameters.description: Acceptable testpoint geometry.

parameters.name: Min Inter-Testpoint Spacing / Component Body Clearance / Board Edge Clearance
parameters.description: Clearance constraints.

parameters.name: Use Grid / Origin / Grid Size / Tolerance
parameters.description: Test-fixture grid.

parameters.name: Allowed Side / Allow Testpoint Under Component
parameters.description: Side and placement constraints.

tools.example: Rule scope All, size 0.9-1.2 mm, spacing 2.54 mm grid, Allowed Side Bottom, Allow Testpoint Under Component enabled (bare board has no parts).
tools.notes: At least one Style rule with scope All must exist for the Testpoint Manager to assign points; DRC tests everything except the Preferred values.

tools.name: Fabrication Testpoint Usage (Testpoint rule)
tools.description: States which nets must (Required), must not (Prohibited) or may (Don't Care) carry fabrication test points, and whether Required means one point per net or a point at every leaf node. Drives the Testpoint Manager's automatic assignment and DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Testpoint > Fabrication Testpoint Usage

parameters.name: Required / Prohibited / Don't Care
parameters.description: Usage mode for nets matching the scope.

parameters.name: Allow multiple testpoints on same net / at each leaf node
parameters.description: Sub-options of Required.

tools.example: Rule InNetClass('NoTest') Prohibited; default rule All Required (single testpoint per net); then Tools > Testpoint Manager > Assign All.
tools.notes: Legacy 'Testpoint Usage' rules from pre-Summer-09 designs migrate to this type.

tools.name: Assembly Testpoint Style (Testpoint rule)
tools.description: Same constraint set as Fabrication Testpoint Style but for in-circuit/flying-probe test of the populated board, so component-body clearance matters and Allow Testpoint Under Component is normally disabled. Assembly test points are reported separately in the Test Point Report output.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Testpoint > Assembly Testpoint Style

parameters.name: Sizes / Clearances / Grid / Allowed Side
parameters.description: As Fabrication Testpoint Style.

tools.example: Size 1.0-1.5 mm, Component Body Clearance 1 mm, Allowed Side Bottom, Allow Testpoint Under Component disabled.
tools.notes: Pads and vias carry separate Fabrication and Assembly testpoint flags in the Properties panel.

tools.name: Assembly Testpoint Usage (Testpoint rule)
tools.description: Required / Prohibited / Don't Care assignment of assembly (ICT) test points per net, independent of the fabrication usage rule so a net can need a bare-board probe but no ICT access, or vice versa.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Testpoint > Assembly Testpoint Usage

parameters.name: Required / Prohibited / Don't Care
parameters.description: Usage mode for the scoped nets.

tools.example: InNetClass('PowerRails') Required; All Don't Care; run Tools > Testpoint Manager with the Assembly tab to allocate.
tools.notes: Outputs: Test Point Report (fabrication/assembly) and Testpoint Manager statistics.

tools.name: Rule scope (Where The Object Matches)
tools.description: Every rule targets objects through a scope expressed as a query. The editor offers All, Net, Net Class, Layer, Net and Layer, Advanced (Query) and Custom Query modes; binary rules (Clearance, Short-Circuit, Creepage, Parallel Segment, Matched Lengths...) have two scopes, unary rules one. The scope is stored as a query string such as InNetClass('DDR') And OnLayer('Top Layer').
tools.usage: Design > Rules > [rule] > Where The Object Matches / Where The First Object Matches, Where The Second Object Matches

parameters.name: Scope mode
parameters.description: All | Net | Net Class | Layer | Net and Layer | Advanced (Query) | Custom Query.

parameters.name: Full Query
parameters.description: The generated or hand-written query expression; Query Builder and Query Helper assist.

tools.example: Clearance rule: first object IsPad And InComponentClass('BGA'), second object IsTrack; Width rule: InDifferentialPairClass('USB').
tools.notes: Scopes are evaluated against objects, so an object matched by several rules of one type is governed by the highest-priority matching rule.

tools.name: Rule priority
tools.description: When several rules of the same type match an object, the rule with the highest priority (priority 1 is highest) wins; the Priorities button in the rules editor reorders rules of a type with Increase/Decrease Priority. Design specific rules with narrow scopes at high priority and the catch-all default rule at the lowest priority.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Priorities... (or drag rules in the tree); Constraint Manager: All Rules view

parameters.name: Priority
parameters.description: Integer order within a rule type; 1 = highest.

tools.example: Width rules: 'Width_DDR' (priority 1, InNetClass('DDR')), 'Width_Power' (2), 'Width' All (3).
tools.notes: Priority does not cross rule types; a Width rule never overrides a Clearance rule.

tools.name: Export Rules / Import Rules (.RUL)
tools.description: Right-click commands in the PCB Rules and Constraints Editor tree that save selected rule types (or all rules) to a .RUL file and load them into another board, letting a company rule set be reused across projects. Imported rules keep their names, scopes and priorities; existing rules with the same name are overwritten after confirmation.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > right-click Design Rules tree > Export Rules... / Import Rules...

parameters.name: Rule types
parameters.description: Checklist of rule categories to export/import.

parameters.name: .RUL file
parameters.description: Rules file path.

tools.example: On the golden board choose Export Rules, select all, save 'Company_4L.RUL'; on a new board Import Rules and pick the same file, then adjust scopes referencing net classes that do not exist yet.
tools.notes: Rules are also carried by PCB templates (.PcbDot) and by the project's Constraint Manager documents when that mode is used.

tools.name: Design > Constraint Manager
tools.description: Spreadsheet-style, document-based editor (Altium Designer 24+) that replaces the PCB Rules and Constraints Editor for projects created with Constraint Management enabled. Views: Clearances (net-class vs net-class matrix per layer), Physical (width, diff-pair gap, via, polygon connect per net/class), Electrical (topology, impedance, layer access, via count, length, stub length) and, from the PCB editor, All Rules for query-based advanced rules. Constraints are captured in the schematic and pushed to the PCB via ECO.
tools.usage: Design > Constraint Manager (schematic or PCB editor); enable with 'Constraint Management' in the Create Project dialog or System.ConstraintManager in Advanced Settings

parameters.name: Clearances / Physical / Electrical / All Rules
parameters.description: The four views (All Rules is PCB-only).

parameters.name: Classes
parameters.description: User-defined net classes, diff pairs, xNets/xSignals grouped as rows.

tools.example: In Physical view set Width Preferred 0.2 mm for class POWER; in Clearances set POWER-to-All 0.3 mm; Design > Update PCB Document to push the rules.
tools.notes: A project uses either the Constraint Manager or the legacy rules editor, decided at creation; the legacy editor is still available for existing projects.

tools.name: Constraints Editor (document-based PCB rules editor)
tools.description: An alternative table-based rules editor that opens as a document tab and groups rules into six sections of increasing priority: Nets, Diff Pairs, xSignals, Polygons, Components and Advanced. Each section is a grid where widths, clearances, via styles and lengths are typed directly per net, class or pair, with Advanced holding query-based rules.
tools.usage: Design > Rules (when the Constraints Editor is enabled for the PCB) or the Constraints Editor tab

parameters.name: Sections
parameters.description: Nets | Diff Pairs | xSignals | Polygons | Components | Advanced.

tools.example: Select the Diff Pairs section, add pair class 'USB', type Width 0.18 mm / Gap 0.15 mm, then run DRC.
tools.notes: Feature availability depends on the release; consult your version's documentation for how to switch between editor styles.

tools.name: Design Rule Checker > Report Options
tools.description: The first page of Tools > Design Rule Check controlling what a batch DRC produces: Create Report File (HTML/TXT/XML), Report PCB Health Issues, Create Violations (markers in the design space), Sub-Net Details, Verify Shorting Copper (net ties), Report Drilled SMT Pads, Report Multilayer Pads with 0 size Hole, Stop when n violations found (default 500), plus split-plane options Report Broken Planes, Report Dead Copper larger than (100 sq mil) and Report Starved Thermals with less than n% available copper (50%).
tools.usage: Tools > Design Rule Check > Report Options > Run Design Rule Check

parameters.name: Create Report File
parameters.description: Write the Design Rule Verification Report.

parameters.name: Create Violations
parameters.description: Add violation markers to the board for the PCB Rules And Violations panel.

parameters.name: Stop when n violations found
parameters.description: Upper limit on reported violations.

tools.example: Enable Create Report File and Verify Shorting Copper, raise the limit to 2000, click Run Design Rule Check, then review the report and the PCB Rules And Violations panel.
tools.notes: Rules To Check page lists every rule with Online and Batch checkboxes per rule type.

tools.name: Design Rule Checker > Rules To Check
tools.description: Grid listing every rule type by category with Online and Batch enable checkboxes, so a rule can exist but be excluded from real-time checking (expensive checks such as Minimum Solder Mask Sliver) while still being verified in batch runs. Right-click offers Online DRC - Used On / Off, Batch DRC - Used On / Off and Used On/Off for all.
tools.usage: Tools > Design Rule Check > Rules To Check (tree: Electrical, Routing, SMT, Mask, Plane, Testpoint, Manufacturing, High Speed, Placement, Signal Integrity)

parameters.name: Online
parameters.description: Check this rule type in real time while editing.

parameters.name: Batch
parameters.description: Check this rule type during Run Design Rule Check.

tools.example: Disable Online for Minimum Solder Mask Sliver and Silk To Solder Mask Clearance to keep editing responsive; keep Batch enabled.
tools.notes: A rule type must be enabled here, the rule itself must be enabled, and Online DRC must be on in Preferences for live checking to occur.

tools.name: Tools > Reset Error Markers
tools.description: Removes all DRC violation markers (the green highlight/overlay graphics) from the PCB without changing the rules, so a fresh batch DRC or online check starts from a clean board. Useful after editing many objects while online DRC is off.
tools.usage: Tools > Reset Error Markers
tools.example: Tools > Reset Error Markers, then Tools > Design Rule Check > Run Design Rule Check to regenerate only current violations.
tools.notes: Clearing markers also empties the PCB Rules And Violations panel's violation list until the next check.

tools.name: Online DRC (real-time design rule checking)
tools.description: Continuous checking of enabled rule types while objects are placed or moved, drawing violation overlays immediately. Requires three things: the Online DRC option in Preferences > PCB Editor > General, the rule type enabled for Online in the Design Rule Checker dialog, and the individual rule enabled. Overlay style is set in PCB Editor > DRC Violations Display.
tools.usage: Preferences > PCB Editor > General > Editing Options > Online DRC

parameters.name: Online DRC
parameters.description: Master switch for live checking.

tools.example: Turn Online DRC on, then drag a track into a pad of another net: the clearance violation is shown at once; hover for the violation details in the Board Insight heads-up display.
tools.notes: Online checks have less granularity than batch DRC (e.g. no Un-Routed Net or Return Path); always run a batch DRC before release.

tools.name: Layer-specific rule values (Layer Attributes Table)
tools.description: Width and Differential Pairs Routing rules include a Layer Attributes grid where Min/Preferred/Max width (and gap) can differ per signal layer, and when Use Impedance Profile is enabled the values are calculated from the Layer Stack Manager impedance profile instead. With multiple layer stacks, Show values for layer stack selects which stack's layers are edited.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Routing > Width or Differential Pairs Routing > Use Impedance Profile / Layer Attributes Table

parameters.name: Use Impedance Profile
parameters.description: Derive widths (and gaps) from a named impedance profile.

parameters.name: Layer Attributes Table
parameters.description: Per-layer Min/Preferred/Max values.

tools.example: Width rule InNetClass('50R') with Use Impedance Profile = 'SE50'; inner layers automatically get the narrower widths computed for their dielectric.
tools.notes: Press 3 during routing to cycle Rule Minimum / Preferred / Maximum / User width for the current layer.
